documents.title: Refill: metformin 500 mg
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request, metformin 500 mg 1 tab twice a day. Last A1c 6.4 on 11/8/24. Approved x90 days with 1 refill. Diabetes f/u due in May; not yet scheduled.

documents.title: Question about my metformin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I took a home pregnancy test last week and it was positive! I already called an OB office and they're getting me in soon. Should I keep taking my metformin until then or stop? I haven't been drinking at all since I found out. Thanks

documents.title: Re: Question about my metformin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Yolanda. Please keep taking the metformin twice a day for now, don't stop it on your own. Bring the bottle to your first OB visit and let them know you have type 2 diabetes; the obstetrics team will take over decisions about your diabetes medicine during the pregnancy. If they want labs or records from us, have them send a request and we'll get them out quickly.

documents.title: Time for your diabetes check
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hello Yolanda, our records show you're due for your diabetes follow-up with the doctor. Reply here or call the office and we'll find a time that works. If you're being seen elsewhere for this, let us know so we can update your chart.

documents.title: Metformin refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Refill request metformin 500 mg BID. Last visit here 11/2024. Pt messaged in May that she is pregnant and being followed by OB. Approved 90-day supply per PCP; recall already sent in June, no reply.

documents.title: Outside obstetrics: prenatal visit 07/18/2025
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics and gynecology group
Prenatal visit, date of service 07/18/2025
Patient: Yolanda Doyle, DOB 06/18/1999, age 26

Gestational age 16 weeks. Here for routine prenatal care. Feels well, no concerns today; pregnancy without problems to this point.

Medical history: type 2 diabetes, good control on metformin.
Surgical history: none.
Medications: metformin; prenatal vitamin one tablet daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with type 2 diabetes; father with hypertension.
Social: never smoker. No alcohol since pregnancy was confirmed. Works as an administrative assistant.

Vitals: BP 120/78, HR 72, temp 37.0 C (98.6 F).
Exam: no abnormal findings. Fetal heart tones heard.

Urine dipstick in clinic: leukocyte esterase 1+; nitrite, protein, glucose and ketones negative. Urine sent for culture.
Culture (final 07/20/2025): greater than 100,000 CFU/mL E. coli.

Assessment: intrauterine pregnancy at 16 weeks. Type 2 diabetes. Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy.

---
Fax cover, 09/30/2025: records per request of primary care. Front desk: placed in chart for PCP review. Problem and medication lists not updated; no visit with us since 11/2024.

events.reason: Patient message: ED visit and admission

documents.title: FYI I'm in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know I went to the ER on Tuesday with a fever and bad pain on my right side. They said it's a kidney infection and kept me in on the OB floor. I'm getting IV antibiotics and feeling a lot better than Tuesday. Baby is moving fine. I'll let you know when I'm home.

documents.title: Re: FYI I'm in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know, Yolanda. Sorry you went through that, and glad you're improving. Follow the hospital team's instructions. Feel free to message any time.

reports.text:
Clinical history: pregnant at about 37 weeks, fever, right flank pain.
Technique: grayscale and color images of both kidneys and the bladder.
Right kidney: hydronephrosis. No calculus. No mass. No perinephric fluid. Normal cortical echogenicity.
Left kidney: normal size and echogenicity. No hydronephrosis, calculus or mass.
Bladder: partially distended, unremarkable. Gravid uterus noted.
reports.conclusion: Right hydronephrosis. No calculi or structural abnormality.

documents.title: Outside ED record: visit 12/16/2025
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Hospital emergency department
ED provider note, date of visit 12/16/2025
Patient: Yolanda Doyle, 26 y/o F, pregnant at approximately 37 weeks

CC: fever, nausea, right flank pain, dysuria.

HPI: Partner brought her in. Three days ago she noticed urinary frequency and pressure above the pubic bone; since then it has progressed to burning with urination, pain in the right flank, nausea, chills and feeling feverish. Denies vaginal bleeding or discharge. Baby moving normally. No urinary infections before this pregnancy. No sick contacts. Had early prenatal care, missed the last two prenatal appointments. Bacteriuria was found on a urine culture at her prenatal visit in July 2025.

PMH: type 2 diabetes; asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy.
PSH: none.
Home meds: metformin 500 mg BID; prenatal vitamin 1 tab daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: T2DM (mother), HTN (father).
Social: never smoker, no alcohol in pregnancy, administrative assistant.

Vitals at triage: T 38.8 C (101.8 F), HR 110, BP 108/70.

Exam: flushed and mildly diaphoretic. Right costovertebral angle tenderness. Abdomen with mild suprapubic tenderness, no rebound, no guarding. Gravid.

UA: leukocyte esterase positive, nitrite positive, WBCs too numerous to count. Urine culture sent.
Renal ultrasound: right-sided hydronephrosis, no stones or structural abnormality.

ED course: IV fluid bolus started. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given.

Impression: acute right pyelonephritis in pregnancy, about 37 weeks.
Disposition: admitted to the obstetric service for IV antibiotics and fetal monitoring.

---
Received by fax 01/27/2026. Front desk: filed to chart, routed to PCP. No discharge summary included.
